rows.answer: For retail reimbursement claims, you have 30 days from the date of discharge [2][4]. For group corporate claims, the reimbursement submission window is 60 days from discharge [5].
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [5][6].
Maternity cover is not available on the Bronze plan [1][4].

Hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and cardiac conditions declared at the proposal stage carry a 36-month waiting period unless Aurora explicitly waives it in writing on the policy schedule [3]. The sources do not state a general waiting period for other pre-existing diseases.
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1].
Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns as of 1 April 2026 [1].

On Aurora Gold, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating to a maximum of 100% [3]. The bonus is not reduced by a claim, and it stops accumulating for that year only [3].
Infertility, assisted reproduction, and IVF are never payable under any Aurora indemnity plan [3].
The cataract surgery limit on Gold is ₹75,000 per eye [2].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome or receive no response within 15 days, you can escalate to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. If Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory, or Aurora has not responded within 30 days of the original complaint, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [3].
Ambulance cover is ₹5,000 per hospitalisation, and it applies to road ambulances only [2].
Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [2].

The free-look period is 15 days from receiving the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [4]. It is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [5].
You get 150 points for completing an annual health check-up [2].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation because of technological advance, and is therefore payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [5]. Out-patient treatment is not a day-care procedure [5].
For an emergency admission under cashless, the hospital must notify Aurora within **24 hours** of admission [2].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a TPA [3].
A facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or 15 in-patient beds elsewhere to qualify as a hospital [2].

No, everything will not be paid [2][3]. Pharmacy and consumables are paid in full, but items tied to the room category are proportionately reduced because the room rent of ₹15,000 per day exceeds your limit of 2% (₹10,000 per day) [1][2][3].

Dependent parents are allowed on Silver (at an extra premium), Gold, and Platinum plans, while Bronze does not allow them [1]. Premium is determined by the age of the eldest member covered [4]. The sources do not state what other changes occur when adding your mother.

Yes, waiting periods already served carry over on portability only up to the sum insured of the previous policy, including its accrued no-claim bonus [3][4]. Any increase or excess in the sum insured is subject to fresh waiting periods [3][4].

To continue cover beyond 90 days, you must add the newborn as a dependent to the policy [3]. You must inform Aurora within 90 days of birth to ensure the addition is guaranteed-issue without medical underwriting [3].
The OPD rider, which covers out-patient benefits, is not available on Bronze [1]. The sources do not state whether out-patient physiotherapy sessions are covered under other benefits.
A claim in any year reduces the accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points, but it does not reset it to zero [3].
On the Gold plan, the maternity limit for a caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 [2]. If the hospital bills ₹1,60,000, you would pay ₹60,000 out of pocket [2].
No, knee and hip joint replacement other than following an accident has a 24-month waiting period [3]. The sources do not state whether it is covered immediately in the event of an accident.
Total discounts are capped at 30% of base premium [3]. The wellness discount is applied last, after the cap, and is the only discount that may exceed it [3].

Cashless can be denied if the hospital is an excluded provider, but denial of cashless is not a rejection of the claim [3][4]. Claims from an excluded provider are payable on reimbursement only if the admission was a genuine emergency and no alternative facility was reachable [1][2].
You have 45 days from the date of the query to respond to a query on a health claim [1], and 30 days from the date of the query to respond to a query on a motor claim [5].
A planned cashless admission must be notified 72 hours before admission [1].
Aurora settles or rejects a complete reimbursement claim within **15 working days** of receiving the last required document [3][4].
The Aurora Gold plan has no co-payment at all ages [3][6]. The sources do not state the names of any other plans that have no co-payment.

The pre-hospitalisation cover is 30 days for the first plan, 45 days for the second plan, 60 days for the third plan, and 90 days for the fourth plan [2]. The post-hospitalisation cover is 60 days for the first plan, 90 days for the second plan, 120 days for the third plan, and 180 days for the fourth plan [2].
Gold removes room-rent sub-limits [5]. Gold also covers dependent parents-in-law [1].

Out-patient dental work is among the items not covered by any plan [3]. Dental treatment and oral surgery are permanently excluded unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [4].

For annual policies, the grace period is 30 days, while for policies paid in instalments, it is 15 days [1]. Renewing after the grace period expires results in the policy being treated as fresh, meaning all waiting periods restart, accumulated no-claim bonuses are lost, and fresh underwriting applies [3].
No, you are not finished [4]. Denial of cashless is not a rejection of the claim, and you can use Route 2 (reimbursement) at non-network hospitals or where cashless was denied [2][4].
Completing the quit-tobacco programme earns 200 points per year [4]. Points convert to a renewal-premium discount at 1,000 points = 5%, capped at 15% [5].

Refractive error correction where the error is less than 7.5 dioptres is permanently excluded [3]. The sources do not state whether a 6 dioptre lasik is covered.
